definition: In mathematics, the spiral optimization (SPO) algorithm is a metaheuristic inspired by spiral phenomena in nature.
details: The first SPO algorithm was proposed for two-dimensional unconstrained optimization based on two-dimensional spiral models. This was extended to n-dimensional problems by generalizing the two-dimensional spiral model to an n-dimensional spiral model. There are effective settings for the SPO algorithm: the periodic descent direction setting and the convergence setting.

explainer.lead: The spiral optimization algorithm is a metaheuristic inspired by spiral phenomena in nature. It matters as a general-purpose optimizer whose behaviour is governed by tunable settings.

tiers.eli5: Search points move in spirals around a centre, closing in on the best spot, the way a spiral pattern narrows toward its middle.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to unconstrained optimization, using the periodic descent direction and convergence settings. A pitfall is that performance depends on choosing those effective settings.
tiers.paperLevel: A metaheuristic based on spiral models; first proposed for two-dimensional unconstrained optimization and extended to n dimensions by generalizing the 2D spiral model. Effective settings include periodic descent direction and convergence settings.

explainer.example: Minimizing a two-dimensional unconstrained function by letting search points follow a 2D spiral model toward the optimum.
